podcast.title: Ability to Fill Stadiums with Guitar Solos
podcast.body: Mios is noted as one of the few bands today capable of filling an 80,000-person stadium and having the audience enjoy an 8-minute guitar solo, which is considered a rare feat in contemporary music. "Son una, casi la única banda bien día, que son capaces de llenar un estadio con 80 mil personas y ponerles un solo de guitarra de 8 minutos y que la gente lo disfrute, que hoy es rarísimo, ¿ver eso?"

podcast.title: Comparison to Queen
podcast.body: Mios's "epic rock" or "opera rock" sound, particularly on albums like "Absolution" and "de sé con lo," has drawn comparisons to Queen from some critics. "Se estaban yendo a ese especie de rock épico o peda rock que a veces recordaba demasiado a Queen."

podcast.title: Conceptual Album Approach
podcast.body: Many Mios albums, starting with "Absolution," were conceived as conceptual albums. However, critics often noted that their conceptual depth was not fully realized when compared to genuinely conceptual works by bands like Pink Floyd or King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard. "Aunque muchos discos de míos son conceptuales, distan mucho de considerar un álbum conceptual propiamente dicho, si lo comparas con álbumes conceptuales de verdad como los que puede hacer Pin Floyd o como álbumes conceptuales modernos como los que puede hacer King Gisa Randalizar Wizard."

podcast.title: Early Vocal and Guitar Style Comparisons to Radiohead
podcast.body: Their debut album "Showbiz" had striking similarities to Radiohead's "OK Computer," from Matt Bellamy's singing style (which later changed significantly) to the "weeping, agonizing, tragic" guitar sound characteristic of "OK Computer." Guitar publications even compared the pedal structures used by both bands. "Los propios míos nunca se han declarado grandes fans de Radiohead de Tom York pero no podemos negar que había parecidos bastante importantes entre los dos discos."

podcast.title: Evolutionary Challenges
podcast.body: While Mios has evolved over the years, they have struggled to truly evolve in a significant way, often falling back on their sonic clichés. "Es una banda que desde siempre ha sido un poco víctima de esos propios clichés sonoros, que si ha sabido evolucionar con los años, pero la que le ha costado mucho evolucionar de verdad."

podcast.title: Great Musicianship
podcast.body: Mios members are widely recognized as great musicians and instrumentalists. "Ellos son unos grandísimos músicos, son unos grandísimos instrumentalistas, no se pueden negar."

podcast.title: Maintaining Guitar Sound in a Dying Market
podcast.body: Mios released guitar-driven albums like "Showbiz" at a time when the guitar sound was considered "officially dead" in the UK after Radiohead's "OK Computer" in the mid-90s. They were one of the few bands keeping the guitar sound alive when it wasn't fashionable. "El sonido guitarrero estaba muriendo poco a poco a mitad de los 90 y al menos en el reino unido, no tanto en Estados Unidos pero sobre todo en el reino unido. Después del loque y computer es como un antesión después. Es la muerte oficial que ha sido el sonido de guitarra."

podcast.title: Mixed Critical Reception
podcast.body: Mios's albums have consistently received mixed reviews, similar to Queen. There are two main critical camps: one that considers them a great rock band at a time when rock was not popular, and another that views them as monotonous, repetitive, and not contributing much new to the music market. "Es curioso porque con esta banda siempre nos ha pasado un poco, pues, como con Quink, que las críticas de sus iscos siempre han sido bastante mixtas."

podcast.title: Paranoid and Surreal Lyrics
podcast.body: Starting from "Black Holes and Rebellations," Matt Bellamy's lyrics began to feature paranoid and surreal themes, discussing conspiracies and aliens. On "de sé con lo," these "paranoid lyrics" were described as "bordering on the ridiculous." "Empieza a esa especie de letras un poco paranoicas y surrealistas que tiene más velami hablando de conspiraciones y de marcianos y de bueno."

podcast.title: Release Coincided with Shifting Trends (Origin of Symetry)
podcast.body: "Origin of Symetry" was released months after Radiohead's "Kid A" sparked a UK craze for experimental electronic progressive rock, and simultaneously with The Strokes' debut, which launched a "garage rock revival." This left Mios somewhat isolated. "Porque justo unos meses antes del lanzamiento Origin of Symetry salía el quide y de Radiohead con lo cual se desatabó en una especie de furor dentro del reino unido por ese rock experimental el electrónico progresivo a raro uno se desatabó en auténtica fiebre después del quide y dentro del reino unido."

podcast.title: Repetitive Sonic Clichés
podcast.body: Mios has often been criticized for getting "stuck in their own clichés," particularly after "Absolution." This includes reiterating an epic sound, heavy piano use, and Matt Bellamy's increasingly forceful vocals, leading to a perception of being un-evolved. "Un poco míos se empezaría a quedar un poco atascado en sus propios cliches."

podcast.title: Self-Production on de resistance
podcast.body: A significant career change for Mios was their decision to self-produce "de resistance," which is considered by many to be a major mistake. This move, without external producers to provide a fresh perspective, led to their sound becoming self-referential and increasingly "more Mios," reinforcing their own stylistic patterns. "En este album también tenemos uno de los más importantes cambios a la carrera de míos que para mucha gente es posiblemente el mayor error de la carrera de míos, que es que en este album han pasado a producirse a sí mismos."

podcast.title: The Guardian's Harsh Review of Origin of Symetry
podcast.body: The album "Origin of Symetry" received a very low rating of "one" from The Guardian newspaper, which considered its guitar sound outdated and boring. "De hecho jamás lo olvidaré y lo tengo que volver a decir en su día de Guardian le dio un uno, un puto, uno que coño me cuentas un uno al origen a Jimmy Hendrix de míos."

podcast.title: Victim of Self-Generated Expectations
podcast.body: A recurring issue throughout Mios's career, particularly for Matt Bellamy, is the problem of being a victim of his own generated expectations. He would often state in interviews, months before an album's release, that it would be groundbreaking, electronic, or radically different, only for the actual release to be perceived as an update of existing sounds. This pattern has led to public disappointment and a loss of credibility. "Uno de los problemas que siempre ha tenido más velami es que es víctima de las propias expectativas que el mismo genera, cuando tú te pasas seis meses antes del lanzamiento del disco, diciendo en las entrevistas que vas a hacer un álbum rompedor, el electrónico, radicalmente distinto a lo que había hecho en ese momento y luego saca eso, la gente se siente excepcionada."
